Prince George's County states the Green Business credit applies to the county portion of tax on qualifying real or personal property for up to five consecutive years, is first-come and subject to funding, requires third-party certification and an October 1 filing, may not be stacked with another local or state property tax credit for the same property, and must be passed through when an eligible lessee is contractually liable for the taxes. The County application supplies the operational percentages: Green Business real property 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% for years 1-5, and Green Business personal property 50% for years 1-5. County high-performance materials supply the new-or-major renovation rates of 25%, 50%, and 75% for 5 years and existing-building O+M rates of 10%, 25%, and 50% for 3 years, with October 1 filing and a $5,000,000 fiscal-year aggregate cap. ([Prince George's County Government][1])

County official page states the credit applies to the County portion of tax on qualifying real/personal property used exclusively by an eligible green business for up to five consecutive tax years, subject to first-come funding and certification. Official County application supplies the rates: real property 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%; personal property 50% for years 1-5. CB-10-2016 supplies five-year/no-stacking/lease-pass-through rules and $1,000,000 annual aggregate cap.

New Mexico TRD describes New Mexico as imposing gross receipts tax on persons engaged in business rather than a conventional retail sales tax. TRD Form RPD-41341 states that, effective July 1, 2007, a deduction from gross receipts tax is available for the sale and installation of a solar energy system. New Mexico 2021 SB0243 amended Section 7-9-112 to provide that, prior to July 1, 2030, receipts from the sale and installation of solar energy systems may be deducted from gross receipts.

Colorado DOR states that the prior heat pump system income tax credit and sales tax exemption expired December 31, 2023, and that beginning January 1, 2024 the new heat pump tax credit is available only to a heat pump tax credit contractor registered with the Colorado Energy Office. DOR DR1322 for 2025 states that the contractor must provide a discount separately stated on the receipt or invoice, that building owners generally cannot claim the credit unless they are registered contractors installing their own heat pump, and that 2025 credit amounts are $500 for heat pump water heaters, $1,500 for air-source or variable refrigerant flow heat pumps, and $3,000 for ground-source, water-source, or combined-source heat pumps. Colorado Revised Statutes Section 39-22-554 provides the 2024-2032 technology-specific amount schedule and unit-count rules. HB26-1289 amended the statutory revenue-forecast reduction provisions and related program administration provisions.

Colorado DOR states that the electric bicycle credit applies for income tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024 and before January 1, 2033 to qualified retailers making retail sales of new qualified electric bicycles in Colorado to qualified purchasers. DOR guidance requires retailer registration, purchaser discount procedures, purchaser affidavit documentation, quarterly reports, income tax return filing, and DR0619 reconciliation. DOR's current table lists 2024 and 2025 amounts of $500 credit, $450 discount, and $50 administrative fee, and 2026 amounts of $250 credit, $225 discount, and $25 administrative fee. Colorado Revised Statutes Section 39-22-555 confirms the retailer-credit structure, purchaser discount, one-discounted-e-bike-per-purchaser-per-calendar-year limitation, refundability, and no carryforward. HB26-1289 amended retailer disqualification, model-information, and forecast-reduction administration provisions.

Official Connecticut legislative materials identify Chapter 203b and PA 26-134 as the current-law update to the municipal uniform solar capacity tax. The official 2025 analysis described the original $10,000 per megawatt, over-1-megawatt, 20-year framework and municipal allocation, form, interest, appeal, and exclusion rules. Official 2026 materials and PA 26-134 snippets show the refresh extending treatment to systems with permission to operate on or after 2025-07-01 and before 2026-07-01, with 19-year treatment beginning 2026-07-01, while retaining the $10,000 per megawatt concept and municipal agreement override mechanics. ([Connecticut General Assembly][3])

ORC 5751.03 imposes CAT at two and six-tenths mills per dollar on taxable gross receipts after subtracting the exclusion amount, applies the full exclusion to the first calendar-quarter return, and carries unused exclusion forward to later quarters in the same year. ([Ohio Laws][12]) ORC Chapter 5751 states that CAT is levied on each person with taxable gross receipts for the privilege of doing business in Ohio, provides quarterly filing mechanics, and requires the fourth-quarter return to adjust over- or under-reported receipts for the calendar year. ([Ohio Laws][13]) Ohio's official CAT information release states that the annual minimum tax is eliminated for periods beginning January 1, 2024, the exclusion is $3,000,000 in 2024 and $6,000,000 in 2025 and thereafter, the 0.26% rate is unchanged, annual filing is eliminated after the 2023 return, taxpayers at or below the threshold are not required to file, and combined/consolidated groups are treated as one taxpayer. ([Cloudinary][14]) Ohio's official update for Q2 2025 confirms the $6,000,000-or-less cancellation message and electronic filing/payment routing through the Ohio Business Gateway. ([GovDelivery][15])

Connecticut DRS Form CT-1120GB states that the Green Building Tax Credit is claimed against Chapter 208 corporation business tax, that DEEP must have approved the application before 2017-12-01, that the credit is allowable costs times the applicable tax-credit percentage, that only 25% of total allowable costs may be claimed in a year, and that no carryforward to 2026 is available on the 2025 form. taxRule.formulaText: Vernon Municipal Code Chapter 5.08 imposes business license taxes on businesses in the City. The general business license tax is based on the average number of employees in the City during the calendar year, using the official employee-band schedule: 0 or 1 employee 750 dollars; 2-10 employees 1,150 dollars; 11-25 employees 1,550 dollars; 26-50 employees 2,150 dollars; 51-75 employees 2,875 dollars; 76-100 employees 3,575 dollars; 101-150 employees 4,250 dollars; 151-200 employees 4,975 dollars; 201-250 employees 5,700 dollars; 251-300 employees 6,425 dollars; 301-400 employees 7,150 dollars; 401-500 employees 7,850 dollars; 501-600 employees 8,600 dollars; 601-700 employees 10,000 dollars; 701-800 employees 11,425 dollars; 801-900 employees 12,850 dollars; 901-1,000 employees 14,275 dollars; 1,001-1,100 employees 15,700 dollars; 1,101-1,200 employees 17,100 dollars; 1,201-1,300 employees 18,500 dollars; 1,301-1,400 employees 19,950 dollars; 1,401-1,500 employees 21,350 dollars; 1,501-1,600 employees 22,775 dollars; 1,601-1,700 employees 24,175 dollars; 1,701-1,800 employees 25,625 dollars; 1,801-1,900 employees 27,025 dollars; 1,901 or more employees 28,450 dollars. Warehousing businesses are taxed in lieu of the employee-based tax at 1,200 dollars for the first 5,000 square feet plus 0.21 dollars per square foot over 5,000 square feet, with a 1,200 dollar minimum and 11,950 dollar maximum. Hazardous waste facilities owe 4 percent of annual gross receipts from inorganic hazardous waste plus 1 percent of annual gross receipts from organic hazardous waste and infectious waste, with a 5,000 dollar minimum. Related hazardous waste is separately measured at 0.30 dollars per gallon, subject to minimum rules; waste-to-energy and solid waste processing or recycling are measured at 0.85 dollars per actual incoming ton, and lead-acid battery recycling is measured at 0.30 dollars per actual incoming ton. Chapter 3.20 separately authorizes special parcel taxes, including a warehouse and distribution parcel tax with a maximum of 20 dollars per 100 square feet of gross land area subject to annual CPI adjustment and City Council proceedings, and a public safety special parcel tax with an FY2023-24 maximum rate of 0.03683 dollars per square foot of taxable parcel area, subject to CPI adjustment and authorized for FY2023-24 through FY2027-28 unless extended by voter approval.

taxRule.formulaText: Iowa supports source-backed sales/use exemptions for specific categories, not a single generic retrofit or energy-efficiency exemption. For verified exempt categories, the exempt amount equals Iowa sales/use tax otherwise due on the qualifying exempt sales price. Iowa Department of Revenue guidance states the general state rate is 6 percent, with local option tax applying where applicable unless otherwise noted. Solar energy equipment is exempt when it is primarily used to collect and convert solar radiation or transform converted solar energy to a storage point or point of use; included examples are panels, inverters, solar roof tiles or shingles, and transmission devices. The solar exemption excludes batteries or other storage points, fencing and other safety or security equipment, equipment not used to collect, convert, or transmit solar energy, and materials used to manufacture, install, or construct solar energy equipment such as racking, pads, and foundations. Wind energy conversion property and materials used to manufacture, install, or construct property that converts wind energy to electrical energy are exempt. Manufacturing and processing exemptions apply only when the item and use satisfy the direct and primary use rules, generally more than half of the use in the exempt activity. taxRule.formulaText: Nevada Renewable Energy Tax Abatement is a project-specific approval workflow, not a generic point-of-sale exemption. Approved project agreements state that the owner must pay all unabated sales/use taxes at the applicable statutory rate. Property tax abatement in the approved agreements equals 55 percent of real and personal property taxes payable by the owner on the facility each year for 20 years.

Unit counts are based on property type: one unit for a single-family residence; number of residential units utilizing the heat pump for multifamily property; total installed nonresidential heating capacity divided by four tons and rounded down; and similar unit or four-ton increment counts for campus and thermal energy network installations. promotedTaxRuleRecords.formulaText: Iowa supports source-backed sales/use exemptions for specific categories, not a single generic retrofit or energy-efficiency exemption. For verified exempt categories, the exempt amount equals Iowa sales/use tax otherwise due on the qualifying exempt sales price. Iowa Department of Revenue guidance states the general state rate is 6 percent, with local option tax applying where applicable unless otherwise noted. Solar energy equipment is exempt when it is primarily used to collect and convert solar radiation or transform converted solar energy to a storage point or point of use; included examples are panels, inverters, solar roof tiles or shingles, and transmission devices. The solar exemption excludes batteries or other storage points, fencing and other safety or security equipment, equipment not used to collect, convert, or transmit solar energy, and materials used to manufacture, install, or construct solar energy equipment such as racking, pads, and foundations. Wind energy conversion property and materials used to manufacture, install, or construct property that converts wind energy to electrical energy are exempt. Manufacturing and processing exemptions apply only when the item and use satisfy the direct and primary use rules, generally more than half of the use in the exempt activity. Labor must be handled under Iowa contractor and taxable-service rules: services on or connected with new construction, reconstruction, alteration, expansion, or remodeling of buildings or structures are exempt, while nonqualifying repair or installation services may remain taxable.

promotedTaxRuleRecords.formulaText: Nevada Renewable Energy Tax Abatement is a project-specific approval workflow, not a generic point-of-sale exemption. The Governor's Office of Energy reviews applications, conducts public hearings, and monitors annual compliance audits. Program requirements include at least 10 years of operation, nameplate capacity of at least 10 megawatts, valid licenses and permits, no prohibited governmental funding, construction workforce and Nevada-residency requirements, capital investment thresholds, wage requirements, health insurance requirements, and no concurrent property, sales, or use tax abatement or exemption. Approved project documents in 2026 show a 3-year sales/use tax abatement term and 20-year property tax abatement term. For the official 2026 Clark County example reviewed, Department of Taxation fiscal notes calculate sales/use tax abatement as eligible purchases multiplied by the combined county sales/use tax rate less the Local School Support Tax rate; 8.375 percent total rate minus 2.600 percent Local School Support Tax equals 5.775 percent abated, while the Local School Support Tax remains due. Approved project agreements state that the owner must pay all unabated sales/use taxes at the applicable statutory rate. Property tax abatement in the approved agreements equals 55 percent of real and personal property taxes payable by the owner on the facility each year for 20 years.
